claim: For every pair of integers \(n,t\ge1\), there exists a literal-systematic code \(E(x)=x\Vert p(x)\) from \(\mathcal A^n\) to \(\mathcal A^{n+t+1}\) that corrects every contiguous deletion burst of length at most \(t\), using \(t+1\) deletion-prone trailer symbols, whenever the alphabet size \(q\) is a power of two with \(q>2(n+t+1)^2+1\); the least such power of two satisfies \(q<4(n+t+1)^2+2\).

correctness.rationale: For each burst length \(r\), a fixed word has at most \(B_r=M-r+1\) descendants, and each descendant has at most \(B_r q^r\) length-\(M\) superwords. Thus \(d \le \sum_{r=1}^{t}B_r(B_rq^r-1) < M^2 q^{t+1}/(q-1)\). If \(q>2M^2+1\), then \(q-1>2M^2\) and \(d<q^{t+1}/2\). Haxell’s independent-transversal criterion applies to parts of size \(q^{t+1}\), producing one word per prefix with no shared burst descendant of any length from one through \(t\). Length-zero correction follows from distinct prefixes. The least power of two above \(2M^2+1\) is below \(4M^2+2\).

evidence: arXiv:2609.38259v1 gives a Haxell benchmark for arbitrary k-deletions using a bound on the full deletion shadow, and a uniform adjacent-burst construction with a quartic-order alphabet for t=2.

The published-finding corpus records 2026/9/18/SCOPE-fixed-qary-deletion-codes-2t-minus-1--0b8ba422fcea and 2026/9/19/SCOPE-qary-deletion-codes-leading-coefficient--51ca25167f9c concern redundancy in bits for q-ary deletion codes, not this literal-prefix/full-symbol resource model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The arbitrary-deletion result has a stronger channel guarantee but a degree bound that counts many noncontiguous deletion patterns, giving an alphabet exponent that grows with \(t\). It does not imply the same \(O((n+t)^2)\) alphabet bound. The new count uses at most \(M-r+1\) burst descendants for each \(r\) and sums the corresponding degrees for \(r=1,\ldots,t\).

For the burst-conflict graph here, \(B_r=M-r+1\) and the degree is bounded by \(M^2\sum_{r=1}^{t}q^r < M^2 q^{t+1}/(q-1)\).

The independent-transversal criterion in DOI:10.1002/jgt.23085 states that a graph of maximum degree d has an independent transversal when every part has size at least 2d; the proof uses a strict inequality.

originality.rationale: The retrieved recent coding paper gives a generic arbitrary-deletion Haxell bound and a uniform adjacent-burst construction, but not the quadratic-alphabet nonuniform bound for all burst lengths. The closest published-finding corpus entries optimize different metrics or different channels. The proof is a new parameter-specific degree estimate, not a claim of a new independent-transversal theorem.
residual_risks: The independent-transversal theorem is existential; no pointwise efficient encoder or uniform family is obtained.

The result is a burst-specific corollary of a classical transversal theorem, and a related prior source already uses that theorem for arbitrary deletion codes; the new point is the smaller burst-specific degree bound.
The bounded published-finding corpus and literature searches may miss an equivalent literal-systematic alphabet-size result.
No optimality claim is made for t+1 trailer symbols when t>2, or for the quadratic alphabet bound.

value.rationale: The alphabet-size exponent drops from the generic arbitrary-deletion Haxell estimate \(O(M^{2t})\) to \(O(M^2)\) for the natural family of contiguous-burst channels, while retaining a literal unchanged prefix and \(t+1\) deletion-prone trailers. At \(t=2\) and \(n\ge3\), three trailers match the known necessary count for the at-most-two-burst systematic model. The tradeoff is useful in the full-symbol metric, although it is nonuniform and does not improve fixed-alphabet bit redundancy.
